subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with structured `RequestError`, or should they keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: The ACP SDK stop-reason union cannot directly represent timeout, rate-limit, context-length, or server-error classes, and switching prompt settlement to JSON-RPC rejection is a client-visible compatibility decision that source review cannot choose alone.

options.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
options.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve Resolved Prompt Responses
options.body: Keep existing resolved `PromptResponse` behavior by default and expose structured failure data through a maintainer-approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Ask For A Replacement
options.body: Keep this issue open and request a narrower maintainer-led or refreshed implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The structured error-kind schema and focused ACP tests trace most directly to this recent ACP error-kind work.
